answer: One concrete defense is stake that vests slowly, like trees maturing in a grove: each identity locks tokens that gain voting weight only after months of consistent honest work, so spinning up a thousand fresh fakes yields almost no influence. A public registry serves as a harbor where honest agents build durable, non-transferable reputation credentials, while long-unused identities decay into harmless relics worthless for sudden coordinated attacks. Cost stays trivial for one real agent but multiplies brutally for a sybil horde.
